# CLI reference

Every command of `agent-whatsapp`, generated from the CLI itself.

The CLI needs no MCP server and no agent. Install `@agentcomms/whatsapp` and run it.

```bash
npx -y @agentcomms/whatsapp <command>          # without installing
npm i -g @agentcomms/whatsapp && agent-whatsapp   # or on the PATH
```

`<angle brackets>` are required, `[square brackets]` optional, `<name...>` repeats. Every command takes
`--json` for a machine-readable envelope, and `--no-color` to drop ANSI codes.

## Exit codes

Scripts should read these rather than parse output.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | it worked |
| `1` | unexpected failure |
| `10` | only a person may do that — add, remove, the chat lists, opening a draft — or a change needs approval |
| `64` | the command was used wrongly |
| `65` | the data given was not usable |
| `66` | what was asked for does not exist |
| `69` | WhatsApp's message store could not be read |
| `75` | temporary; retrying later is reasonable |
| `77` | macOS needs the person to allow access to WhatsApp’s data (Full Disk Access) |
| `78` | a configuration problem, including a Node older than 22.16, which has no complete `node:sqlite` |

## Commands

| Command | What it is for |
|---|---|
| [`add`](#agent-whatsapp-add) | give WhatsApp for Mac's message store a name, as organisation/whatsapp — a person does this |
| [`remove`](#agent-whatsapp-remove) | forget an account, its chat lists and its local index — a person does this; WhatsApp's own store is not touched |
| [`allow`](#agent-whatsapp-allow) | let agents see this chat; once any chat is allowed, agents see only allowed chats — a person does this |
| [`deny`](#agent-whatsapp-deny) | hide this chat from agents entirely: not listed, searched, read or drafted to — a person does this |
| [`clear`](#agent-whatsapp-clear) | take a chat off both lists, or with no chat, empty them — a person does this |
| [`status`](#agent-whatsapp-status) | what is set up, whether each store can be read, and what the index holds |
| [`sync`](#agent-whatsapp-sync) | copy WhatsApp's store privately, check it, and rebuild the local index from the copy |
| [`chats`](#agent-whatsapp-chats) | chats, most recent first, as of the last sync; status updates only with --kind status |
| [`read`](#agent-whatsapp-read) | one chat, newest first: by the id `chats` shows, or by phone number |
| [`search`](#agent-whatsapp-search) | words, in text, captions, file names, sender names and chat names, as of the last sync |
| [`draft`](#agent-whatsapp-draft) | a message as a link that opens WhatsApp with it filled in — you press send; nothing is sent here. <to> is a phone number or an id `chats` shows |
| [`approve`](#agent-whatsapp-approve) | approve a change at this terminal — registering or pruning this server — by reading it and typing the code back; WhatsApp never sends, so there is no message to approve |
| [`mcp`](#agent-whatsapp-mcp) | run the MCP server on stdio, for a coding agent to connect to |

### `agent-whatsapp add`

give WhatsApp for Mac's message store a name, as organisation/whatsapp — a person does this

```
agent-whatsapp add [options] <name>
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--source <path>` | a ChatStorage.sqlite elsewhere, e.g. WhatsApp Business’s; the default is WhatsApp for Mac’s | — |

### `agent-whatsapp remove`

forget an account, its chat lists and its local index — a person does this; WhatsApp's own store is not touched

```
agent-whatsapp remove [options] <name>
```

### `agent-whatsapp allow`

let agents see this chat; once any chat is allowed, agents see only allowed chats — a person does this

```
agent-whatsapp allow [options] <chat>
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | which WhatsApp account, as `organisation/whatsapp` | — |

### `agent-whatsapp deny`

hide this chat from agents entirely: not listed, searched, read or drafted to — a person does this

```
agent-whatsapp deny [options] <chat>
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | which WhatsApp account, as `organisation/whatsapp` | — |

### `agent-whatsapp clear`

take a chat off both lists, or with no chat, empty them — a person does this

```
agent-whatsapp clear [options] [chat]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | which WhatsApp account, as `organisation/whatsapp` | — |

### `agent-whatsapp status`

what is set up, whether each store can be read, and what the index holds

```
agent-whatsapp status [options]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | only this account | — |
| `--no-check` | do not open the WhatsApp store to test access; report only what is recorded | — |

### `agent-whatsapp sync`

copy WhatsApp's store privately, check it, and rebuild the local index from the copy

```
agent-whatsapp sync [options]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | which WhatsApp account, as `organisation/whatsapp` | — |

### `agent-whatsapp chats`

chats, most recent first, as of the last sync; status updates only with --kind status

```
agent-whatsapp chats [options]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | which WhatsApp account, as `organisation/whatsapp` | — |
| `--limit <n>` | how many: 1 to 500 | `"50"` |
| `--kind <kind>` | only one kind of chat (choices: "direct", "hidden-number", "group", "status", "broadcast", "channel", "unknown") | — |

### `agent-whatsapp read`

one chat, newest first: by the id `chats` shows, or by phone number

```
agent-whatsapp read [options] <chat>
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | which WhatsApp account, as `organisation/whatsapp` | — |
| `--limit <n>` | how many messages: 1 to 200 | `"50"` |
| `--before <id>` | older than this message: the `next` value of an earlier read | — |

### `agent-whatsapp search`

words, in text, captions, file names, sender names and chat names, as of the last sync

```
agent-whatsapp search [options] <query>
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | which WhatsApp account, as `organisation/whatsapp` | — |
| `--chat <chat>` | only in this chat | — |
| `--sender <name>` | only from senders whose name contains this | — |
| `--kind <kind>` | only in one kind of chat; status updates are searched only when asked for (choices: "direct", "hidden-number", "group", "status", "broadcast", "channel", "unknown") | — |
| `--limit <n>` | how many: 1 to 100 | `"20"` |

### `agent-whatsapp draft`

a message as a link that opens WhatsApp with it filled in — you press send; nothing is sent here. <to> is a phone number or an id `chats` shows

```
agent-whatsapp draft [options] <to> <text>
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | the account the chat belongs to, as `organisation/whatsapp`; its allow and deny lists apply (without it, every account’s do) | — |
| `--open` | open the link in WhatsApp now (a person only; an agent gives the link to the person) | `false` |

### `agent-whatsapp approve`

approve a change at this terminal — registering or pruning this server — by reading it and typing the code back; WhatsApp never sends, so there is no message to approve

```
agent-whatsapp approve [options] <approvalId>
```

### `agent-whatsapp mcp`

run the MCP server on stdio, for a coding agent to connect to

```
agent-whatsapp mcp [options] [command]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | pin the server to one account; every tool then acts on it and no other | — |

### `agent-whatsapp mcp install`

register this server with an MCP client, and prove it starts — a change the person approves

```
agent-whatsapp mcp install [options]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--client <client>` | which client to register with (choices: "claude-code", "claude-desktop", "codex", "cursor", "gemini", "vscode", "json") | — |
| `--name <name>` | the name the client will show: 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens | `"whatsapp"` |
| `--account <name>` | pin the server to one account | — |
| `--launcher <launcher>` | how the server is started (choices: "managed", "npx", "local") | — |
| `--no-verify` | do not start the server to check the entry works | — |
| `--force` | replace this server's own earlier entry — this is how you upgrade | `false` |
| `--print` | only print what would be written | `false` |
| `--approval <approvalId>` | register the server this approval was given for | — |

### `agent-whatsapp mcp prune`

remove managed runtimes that no client config it can read names, no printed entry names, and no process runs

```
agent-whatsapp mcp prune [options]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | only say what would be removed | `false` |
| `--include-printed` | also remove runtimes kept only because an entry for them was printed (--client json, --print), once those entries are gone | `false` |
| `--approval <approvalId>` | remove the runtimes this approval was given for | — |
